title: The Spinewright's Lantern (Hiillos) — As Legend Imagines It
purpose: A stylized 'legend' image of the Spinewright's Lantern for the lantern's KB gallery: how the faithful of the Light glorify the relic, NOT how it truly looks. The deliberate counterpart to the grounded true-object plate (config/image/prompts/spinewrights-lantern-reference-plate-prompt.json). The gap between this glory and the humble real ember is the point.
render_note: INTENTIONALLY BYPASSES the house style. This is an in-world Renaissance/Baroque oil painting, not a grounded campaign illustration, so it is generated by passing the prompt straight to generate_image.py (no compose_image_prompt house-style injection) with the true-object plate as an --image likeness reference so the depicted lantern matches its canonical design.
subject: The ward-lantern Hiillos, suspended UNHELD in its own glory at the center of an altarpiece — no figure holds, carries, or touches it (the Spinewright stays anonymous). It matches the reference plate's design (tall slender gothic body of dark iron and pale stone with tarnished gold, domed shingled top, forged carry-ring, arched openwork, enclosed faceted ember housing), here rendered radiant and glorious, blazing with warm golden light.
the_miracle: Golden god-rays stream from the lantern's heart, driving back a palpable darkness whose shadowy fiends recoil at the margins. One or two armed archangels drive the dark back; idealized faithful kneel below in reverence, hands raised, gazing up — never touching the relic.
the_spines_tribute: Behind and below, a range of jagged pale-grey mountains recedes into golden haze, beacon-towers (the Spines) crowning the peaks, each topped with the same warding light as the lantern — framing the lantern as the portable kin of those great mountaintop works. Mountains with towers on their summits, never a fortified wall or castle battlement.
style: High Renaissance / Baroque old-master oil on aged panel: rich chiaroscuro, deep shadow against warm gilded highlights, luminous glazes, reverent altarpiece composition; fine craquelure and darkened varnish, the patina of a centuries-old masterwork.
do_not_include: any figure holding, grasping, carrying, lifting, or touching the lantern; a hand on or reaching for it
a fortified city wall, castle battlement, or fortress wall (the Spines crown a mountain range)
a plain studio backdrop; any modern, photographic, or CGI-rendered look; glossy plastic surfaces
any text, lettering, numbers, painted frame, or border within the image
redesigning or simplifying the lantern away from the reference plate
